Depot, contractor or ship repair yard: SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 for Jacksonville NDT technicians

Naval aviation shapes Jacksonville's aerospace NDT far more than airline or factory work does. Fleet Readiness Center Southeast at NAS Jacksonville, which the Navy describes as the largest maintenance, repair, overhaul and technical services provider in Northeast Florida and Southeast Georgia, inducted its first F-35 for depot work in August 2024 and took in its first F135 engine power module the same week. Around the depot, contractors at Cecil Airport, ship repairers on the St. Johns River and the city's industrial plants each answer the certification question their own way. For how the two documents compare in general, read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A.

Inside the Navy depot

Military and civil service NDT personnel at the depot are qualified to Navy directives and to the technical requirements of the aircraft and engine programs they support. The individual does not choose a scheme there. If you apply, the hiring organization will tell you what qualification it expects, and it may train you to its own requirements after you join.

At a defense aerospace contractor

Cecil Airport lists Boeing among its tenants, modifying F/A-18 Hornets for the Navy and Marine Corps and serving as a national center for Hornet and Super Hornet component structural repair. On defense aircraft programs, primes have written NAS 410 into supplier quality clauses ever since it took over from MIL-STD-410, so contractors and sub-tier shops around Cecil should expect to meet it. Each company's own written practice still names the standard and revision that apply to you, and its Level 3 is the person to ask.

Civil aircraft maintenance

Repair stations working on civil aircraft follow the personnel standard written into their own manuals and customer contracts. The FAA does not certify NDT personnel; Advisory Circular 65-31B lists NAS 410, ATA Specification 105, SNT-TC-1A and several other standards as acceptable, so two Jacksonville stations can legitimately use different documents.

On ships, bridges and plant equipment

Ship repair contractors serving Naval Station Mayport and the river yards add NAVSEA requirements to their own written practices. Port cranes and terminals, rail equipment, bridge steel and utility outages run under written practices built on SNT-TC-1A, because the AWS, ASME and owner specifications behind that work call for it. Many Jacksonville technicians hold certifications from both sides over a career, one employer at a time.

Moving from the river to a hangar job

An SNT-TC-1A Level II earned on hull plate or terminal piping is good evidence, but it does not satisfy a NAS 410 requirement on its own. The receiving shop's Responsible Level 3 (RL3) decides what earlier training, experience and examinations to credit, and certifies you again. Penetrant and magnetic particle are where the gap usually shows, since NAS 410 calls for more formal, documented training in those surface methods; eddy current is often new as well. Keep course outlines with recorded hours, a signed experience log by method, examination results and a current vision record. A college course such as FSCJ's introductory NDT class counts as training evidence only if its outline and hours are on paper.

For Jacksonville quality managers

Shops that take defense aerospace orders alongside marine or industrial work should keep the programs clearly separate and print the governing standard and revision on each certification. Plan the move to NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025, when customers require it. Nadcap AC7114 and prime auditors pick inspectors and trace their files to evidence. Atlantis prepares and reviews NAS 410 audit documentation for your RL3 to approve, and aviation NDT consulting covers written practices built on SNT-TC-1A and aligned to the customer's flow-down and Nadcap AC7114.

Atlantis's role on the First Coast

Atlantis training is based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A: theory online at your own pace with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, practice in the Practical NDT simulator, and hands-on work plus the practical examination at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Jacksonville. For aircraft work, see aviation NDT training and the method pages on eddy current testing in aviation and penetrant testing in aviation. First Coast plants and terminals can use Atlantis for UT, MT, PT and VT inspection.

Spelled out for Jacksonville: Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3. Before enrolling, ask the employer's RL3 whether SNT-TC-1A-based training will be credited toward a NAS 410 certification; the decision is theirs.
